claim_one_line: THE END'S CHOICE (the owner's approved genesis-side question, 2026-09-30: does the swap P act on B1500's choice at a cusp point the way it acts on the order bit, and does anything in the architecture fix that choice?). Decided at design time, so not sealed (the record's rule for theorems, as B1396, B1500, B1502). T1: the order bit is not a property of the oriented manifold -- L^-1 (LR) L = RL with det L = +1, and four of the eight isometries between b++LR and b++RL (both m004) preserve orientation (B979's finding, orientation made explicit) -- so no datum at a cusp point depends on it; at the isometry level the swap induces the fibre's reflection (-,+,-) in main's B1324 dictionary, and the characters that act on an existing end choice are the Higgs class's sign (the frame, where orientation acts on nothing: intersection homology is orientation-free and Pantev-Wijnholt's W = int CS changes sign under reversal, absorbed by U(1)_R) or the mirror s_m s_l (with a G2 orientation, where orientation reversal acts as parity), never the swap's own sign where a choice exists. T2: the lines every isometry of m004 fixes are exactly the meridian and the longitude = the homological longitude = the fibre's boundary; the two symmetric self-dual completions of the genesis's marked point fill to S^3 and to the Sol torus bundle (P019's F6 sibling); m003: (1, 0) and its fibre boundary (1, -2), filling to H_1 = Z/10 and to the closed torus bundle of -LR (Z/5 + Z). T3: a finite group of lattice automorphisms fixes a line iff it has no rotation of order 3, 4 or 6 (all 26 subgroups of D4 and D6); at a cusp point a rotation fixes, the self-conjugate (gauge) sector has no symmetric completion and every symmetric completion of a charged pair is chiral; so a completion of the whole theory preserved by every isometry exists iff no cusp point is rotated, and is then available non-chiral -- symmetry never forces a chiral end; at a rotated hexagonal point the completion picks one of the three root lines the rotation permutes (B1502's three smooth phases). Census (own code; SnapPy isometries; each of 3024 cusp-fixing maps checked as a similarity of the flat cusp lattice; B1369's instrument agreeing on all 99 family members): 209 members (B1186's 99 arithmetic, cube~3.24, B1399's 109 covers), 398 cusp points; 25 rotated points on 10 members, orders 3 and 6 only, all hexagonal, the root lines permuted everywhere; every cusp rotated on 7 members (5 chiral: m202, s959, v3551, o9_40999, o10_150726, where symmetry alone would force the charged ends chiral but the gauge sector's end then has no symmetric completion); the 199 unrotated members all admit a symmetric self-dual completion; with the trivial vacuum a symmetric chiral completion is allowed on all 199 in the frame and on exactly the 123 chiral ones with a G2 orientation (on the 76 amphichiral ones, m004 and m003 among them, the orientation-reversing isometries pair lower with upper: 72 allow no chiral end at all, 4 only pairs with net zero). Reading: the end's chirality is not supplied by the architecture -- its selectors cannot carry it, its fibration picks the non-chiral completions of the puncture, and its symmetries permit a non-chiral completion or none. sL-3's second closing condition, at the ends; whether the completion carries a G2 orientation is the physical question left (sL-8). No physics crossed. 0 of 19.
